reason: No cited evidence is provided to support any of the key premises. The claims about nanoparticle dispersion, room-temperature deformation mechanisms, high-temperature tribochemical glaze formation, and the resulting friction/wear performance are entirely unsupported by specific prior results.
premises: Y2O3 nanoparticles can be uniformly dispersed in a CoCrFeNi matrix at 0.25–0.5 wt%
Dispersed Y2O3 nanoparticles impede dislocation motion and promote stable shear localization at room temperature, reducing friction
Nanoparticle/matrix interfaces catalyze tribochemical reactions to rapidly form a protective, lubricious nanocrystalline oxide glaze layer at high temperatures
This glaze layer minimizes adhesive and oxidative wear across the full temperature range
The intervention yields 1–2 orders of magnitude lower wear rate and consistently low friction vs. unmodified CoCrFeNi from RT to 800 °C
